key_insight: Chemical gradients in porous and crowded media can actively transport colloids and droplets by diffusiophoresis and diffusioosmosis, sometimes dominating classical filtration and dispersion mechanisms.
engineering_relevance: Controlling solute gradients offers a new lever for enhancing contaminant removal, managing clogging, and tuning transport in soils, filters, tissues, hydrogels, and microfluidic porous devices.
method: Reviews the physical origin of chemical gradients in complex media.
Combines minimal diffusiophoresis/diffusioosmosis theory with classical colloid transport concepts.
Synthesizes experimental platforms and recent pore-scale studies on dead-end pores and flowing pathways.
evidence_signal: The abstract highlights recent experimental and theoretical results showing that diffuse solute fronts can prolong phoretic forcing in dead-end pores and alter breakthrough and dispersion by orders of magnitude.
watch_item: Predictions may depend strongly on geometry, solute chemistry, and the transition from 2D algebraic mixing to 3D chaotic mixing, so scaling from micromodels to real porous media needs care.
paper_title: Diffusiophoretic transport of colloids and emulsions in complex environments
